CLAIM AS WRITTEN:  
"which is exactly the family built in [[fs-pointwise-convergence-implies-uniform-convergence-on-compact-sets]]: each $f_k$ is continuous, and $(f_k)$ converges pointwise to the constant function $\mathbf{0}$, which is continuous."  
WHY IT FAILS:  
The provided text of the cited dependency states only the false claim and mentions that a refutation writes down the moving spike explicitly. It does **not** itself assert that the spikes are continuous, that they converge pointwise, or that their limit is continuous. The citation therefore points to an item that (as quoted) does not make the claimed statement.  
WHAT WOULD FIX IT:  
Either remove the citation and add a short direct verification (the formulas and the other cited lemmas suffice) or include the actual refutation steps from that item so the cited text supplies the needed properties.

### FINDING 2 — NONFATAL — location: [L2]
CLAIM AS WRITTEN:  
"$0 \le f_k(t) \le 1$ for every $t \in I$: on $[0,a_k]$ the value $t/a_k$ lies between $0$ and $1$, on $[a_k,2a_k]$ the value $2 - t/a_k$ does, and on $[2a_k,1]$ it is $0$ ([[def-max-min]], [[lem-finite-set-has-max]])."  
WHY IT FAILS:  
The cited items define maximum/minimum and prove that every nonempty finite set of reals has a max and a min. They do **not** make any claim about the specific inequality $0 \le f_k(t) \le 1$. The citation is to items that do not state the displayed fact.  
WHAT WOULD FIX IT:  
Remove the citation or replace it with a simple appeal to the order properties of $\mathbb{R}$ and the positivity of $a_k$.
